list.item: Gout with recurrent flares, mostly in the right big toe, without tophi; synthetic modern diagnosis linked to his documented gout: active, confirmed [S]
Chronic kidney disease stage G3a A1: active, confirmed [S]

Start allopurinol 100 mg daily and raise it by 100 mg every 2 to 5 weeks until serum urate is below 6 mg/dL; HLA-B*58:01 testing is not indicated, because he is not of Southeast Asian or African ancestry. Guideline: 2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout (2020) [S]

Colchicine 0.6 mg daily for three to six months as flare prophylaxis; treat flares with a short prednisone course or extra colchicine, and avoid NSAIDs because of chronic kidney disease. Guideline: 2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout (2020); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension, chronic kidney disease, and benign prostatic hyperplasia monographs (2026) [S]

Replace hydrochlorothiazide with losartan, which lowers blood pressure and slightly lowers urate; check potassium and creatinine 2 to 4 weeks after starting. Guideline: 2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout (2020); 2017 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2017); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension, chronic kidney disease, and benign prostatic hyperplasia monographs (2026) [S]

Urology referral to confirm and remove the bladder stone, look for bladder outlet obstruction and other causes of hematuria, and advise on stone prevention. Guideline: Medical Management of Kidney Stones: AUA Guideline (2014, amended 2019); EAU Guidelines on Urolithiasis (including bladder stones) (2025); Management of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Attributed to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: AUA Guideline (2023 amendment) [S]

CMID kidney and blood pressure monitoring: blood pressure every visit; eGFR and urine albumin yearly at G3a A1; calcium, phosphate, and PTH at baseline; hemoglobin and the kidney failure risk equation yearly; statin for age over 50 with eGFR below 60; medication review for NSAIDs every visit. Guideline: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension, chronic kidney disease, and benign prostatic hyperplasia monographs (2026) [S]

Limit alcohol, especially beer and spirits, and purine-rich meat, organ meat, and shellfish; avoid sugar-sweetened drinks; aim for gradual weight loss and daily walking. Guideline: 2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout (2020) [S]
